title: The data subject request operations, schemas, record code and person reference are not in any source
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.27); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1, T-A); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-016)
description: No source declares an operation, a schema or a field set for a data subject request: FSD A2.27 names the journey, two validation rules and BR-P4-027, and the P4 appendix T-A lists roles, the access log, reference loads, rule packages and break-glass and no data subject request operation. The legacy story names two rule-version endpoints instead. The four operations, the three schemas, the state set, the record code of a step and the shape of the person reference are therefore fixed by RWB-P4-E8016-CON on the assumption in force.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.27.4.1 carries AC-P4-027-01 and no operation; TSD P4 v3 T-A.1 carries API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is a data subject request; the legacy Endpoints table lists POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and its approve path
area: P4 rwb-access, data subject request register
owner_role: Solution architect, with the compliance and PDPA officer
proposed: Fix the four operations, the three schemas, the state set, the record code of a data subject request and the person-reference shape in RWB-P4-E8016-CON and confirm them with Compliance and the decision-record library owner before the baseline tag.

title: The statutory period is not set and the decision that would set it is open
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4.md (NFR-043); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T7)
description: NFR-043 states the target as the statutory period, not set as a working service level, with the status Open, DL26, and REQ-S8-007 uses the same phrase. No source gives the length of the period, its unit, its working-day rule or the name of the parameter row that would hold it, and no source states whether the clock runs from receipt, from the business date or from acknowledgement. The due date is therefore a parameter row of rwb-case read through DP-06 whose name and value are unknown until Compliance sets them.
evidence: Program BRD v4 NFR-043 target column: statutory period, not set as a working service level, status Open, DL26; TSD P4 v3 T7 NFR-043 identical; FSD P4 v3 A2.27.4.1 names no period
area: PDPA statutory period, DP-06 parameter of rwb-case
owner_role: Compliance and PDPA officer, with the rwb-case parameters owner
proposed: Close DL26 and enter the statutory period as a parameter row of rwb-case with its unit and its working-day rule; the story reads the row through DP-06 and holds no value.

title: Where a correction is applied and where an erasure removes a field are not assigned
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.27, A2.5); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T3.1 masking_rule)
description: A correction and an erasure both act on data this service does not hold: the personal field lives in rwb-source-data and rwb-case and the document lives in rwb-document. No source says which service applies a corrected value, which service removes or blanks an erased field, which field ids an erasure covers by default, or how a masking row relates to the retention classes of P5 and to the case hold of R-UNI-11. This story records the decision and writes the masking rows of an erasure against the policy of RWB-P4-E1037-APP.
evidence: FSD P4 v3 A2.27 has one main success flow and no alternate flow; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 declares masking_rule with unmasked and masking_version and no consumer; the ownership map puts the case and the source fields in P3 and P1 and the retention classes in the P5 work
area: Correction and erasure execution across P1, P3, P5 and P4
owner_role: Solution architect, with the data steward
proposed: Assign the application of a correction and the removal of an erased field to the owning services, fix the default field set of an erasure and state the precedence between a masking row, a retention class and a case hold.

title: The access log cannot be filtered by case id and the workbench-wide evidence belongs to another service
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T-A API-P4-008); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.7); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slides 14 and 28)
description: API-P4-008 declares the query user, from, to, event, page and size and no case id, while the evidence of an access request is per case: FSD A2.7 writes each read with its case id and the field ids returned. The workbench-wide answer across the other eighteen services is the central ledger query of P7, and no source says which of the two an access request is answered from or how the two are joined without copying personal data. This story answers from its own access entries through the owner read with a case-id filter the contract fixes.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T-A.2 API-P4-008 request row: query user, from, to, event, page, size; FSD P4 v3 AC-P4-007-01 writes the case id and the field ids of a read; Architecture v5 slide 14 puts no inbound event on rwb-access and slide 28 makes P7 the workbench-wide query
area: Access evidence for a data subject request
owner_role: Solution architect, with the access-log owner and the P7 ledger owner
proposed: Add the case-id filter to the access-log read and state whether a cross-service access request is answered from the P7 ledger query, with the join named and no personal value copied.

title: The legacy story carries a rule-change capability it does not have
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-016); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (A2.18, A2.21, A2.27)
description: The legacy story names the rule-version endpoints POST /api/recovery/v1/admin/rule-versions and its approve path, the rule_row data row and SCR-39 Rules and parameters, and its two criteria say the result is written to the decision log with the rule version. A data subject request loads no rule version and carries no rule version of its own, so the endpoints, the rule_row row and the SCR-39 reference are a copied apparatus of the rule-change stories; the rule version named by AC1 is read here as the version of the parameter row in force.
evidence: Legacy Endpoints table lists the two rule-version paths; legacy Data table lists rule_row DF-REF-001 to DF-REF-015; FSD A2.18 and A2.21 are the rule-change and template features; FSD A2.27 declares one main success flow and no rule load
owner_role: Business analyst, with the compliance and PDPA officer
proposed: Keep the capability, the two criteria, the five messages and the four test ids, leave the rule-version endpoints and the rule_row row with RWB-P4-E8007-APP and RWB-P4-AD011-APP, and read the rule version of AC1 as the version of the parameter row in force.

title: The fraud flag has no field on the case the P3 contract returns
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P3 Case and workflow v3.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-018)
description: The referral is triggered where the fraud rules require it, and the case is read through the P3 contract by its case number. title: No owner, protocol or result channel exists for the Aric interface
source: 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench API Specification v4.yaml
description: Aric is an outside fraud system. No service in the ownership map owns it, no operation of Aric appears in the API specification or in the Arch v5 catalogue, and its protocol, its credentials, its timeout and the channel on which its result arrives are not specified. The referral is therefore declared as an external dependency and called through one adapter that is faked in every test, and the second external dependency is a gap rather than a metadata value.
evidence: The ownership map lists no Aric owner; API Specification v4 contains no Aric path; Architecture v5 names the outside systems and does not name Aric
owner_role: Solution architect, with the integration owner of rwb-integration (P2)
proposed: Assign the Aric interface to one owner, fix its protocol, credentials, timeout and result channel, and state whether the referral is a direct adapter call or a rwb-integration file, so the external dependency can be recorded against the story.

title: The legacy trigger of the referral has no counterpart in the target service
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E8-018); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md (T5.3); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md (slide 14)
description: The legacy criterion opens with the trigger of the feature, described as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer. TSD P4 v3 T5.3 declares no event for the module and Architecture v5 slide 14 makes rwb-access a reference-data owner with no inbound event, and no source gives the referral a Schedule. The referral is therefore raised by one call from the case or the fraud screen and no subscription, inbox row or Schedule is declared.
evidence: TSD P4 v3 T5.3 events table row None; Architecture v5 slide 14 IN line lists the four REST reads and says events none; FSD P4 v3 A2.29.2 step 1 names a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer
owner_role: Solution architect
proposed: State that a referral is raised by an explicit call from the case screen or by the fraud rule verdict handler of rwb-decision, and declare no event, no inbox row and no Schedule for the capability.
